problems.constraints:
- `1 <= m, n <= 6`
- `1 <= word.length <= 15`
- `board` and `word` consist of English letters
problems.statement:
Given an `m x n` grid of letters and a string `word`, return `true` if `word` can be traced through the grid by moving between horizontally or
vertically adjacent cells, using each cell at most once.
problems.title: Word Search

problems.constraints:
- the tree has between `1` and `10^4` nodes
- `0 <= Node.val <= 10^4`
problems.statement:
Houses form a binary tree; each node's value is the money in that house. A thief can't rob two houses that are directly linked (a parent and
its child) on the same night. Return the maximum amount the thief can rob.
problems.title: House Robber III

problems.statement:
Place `n` queens on an `n x n` chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no two share a row, column or diagonal). Return the number
of distinct placements.
problems.title: N-Queens II

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= s.length <= 20`
- `s` consists of digits
problems.statement:
A valid IPv4 address has four integers between `0` and `255` separated by dots, with no leading zeros (`"0.1.2.201"` is valid,
`"01.1.2.3"` isn't). Given a string of digits `s`, return every valid address that can be formed by inserting three dots into `s` (without
reordering or removing digits), in any order.
problems.title: Restore IP Addresses

problems.statement:
`image` is a grid of pixel colours. Starting from pixel `(sr, sc)`, repaint it and every pixel connected to it horizontally or vertically
through pixels of the **same original colour** with `color`. Return the modified image.
problems.title: Flood Fill

problems.constraints:
- `grid` is `3 x 3`
- `0 <= grid[i][j] <= 9`, and the values add up to 9
problems.statement:
A `3 x 3` grid holds exactly 9 stones in total; `grid[i][j]` is the number of stones in a cell (a cell may hold several). In one move you may
take a single stone and move it to an adjacent cell (sharing a side). Return the minimum number of moves needed so that every cell holds
exactly one stone.
problems.title: Minimum Moves to Spread Stones Over Grid

tests.explanation: Moving one stone from (2,1) up and right takes 3 moves.

problems.constraints:
- `board` is `9 x 9`; each cell is a digit or `'.'`
- the puzzle has exactly one solution
problems.statement:
Fill in the empty cells (`'.'`) of the `9 x 9` Sudoku `board` **in place** so that every row, every column and every one of the nine `3 x 3`
boxes contains each digit `1`-`9` exactly once. Every test puzzle has exactly one solution.
problems.title: Sudoku Solver

tests.explanation: A classic puzzle; the filled board is the only solution.

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= matchsticks.length <= 15`
- `1 <= matchsticks[i] <= 10^8`
problems.statement:
`matchsticks[i]` is the length of stick `i`. Using **every** stick exactly once, without breaking any, can you form a square? Sticks may be
joined end to end along a side. Return `true` if a square can be made.
problems.title: Matchsticks to Square

problems.constraints: - `0 <= turnedOn <= 10`
problems.statement:
A binary watch has 4 LEDs for the hour (0-11) and 6 LEDs for the minute (0-59); each LED is one bit of the value. Given how many LEDs are
on, `turnedOn`, return every time the watch could be showing, in any order. Hours have no leading zero (`"1:00"`, not `"01:00"`) and
minutes always have two digits (`"10:02"`, not `"10:2"`).
problems.title: Binary Watch

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= transactions.length <= 8`
- `0 <= from_i, to_i < 12`, `from_i != to_i`
- `1 <= amount_i <= 100`
problems.statement:
`transactions[i] = [from_i, to_i, amount_i]` means person `from_i` gave `amount_i` dollars to person `to_i`. Return the minimum number of
new transactions needed so that everyone ends up even (each person has received exactly as much as they gave).
problems.title: Optimal Account Balancing

tests.explanation: Person 1 pays 5 to person 0 and 5 to person 2.
One transfer: person 1 pays 4 to person 0.

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= s.length <= 16`
- `s` consists of lowercase English letters
problems.statement:
Split `s` into non-empty substrings that concatenate back to `s`, with all the substrings **distinct**. Return the largest possible number
of substrings.
problems.title: Split a String Into the Max Number of Unique Substrings

tests.explanation: a, b, ab, c, cc: five pieces.
"aa" can't be split into distinct pieces.

problems.constraints:
- the tree has between `1` and `100` nodes
- `-100 <= Node.val <= 100`
problems.statement:
Return every root-to-leaf path of the binary tree, in any order. Write a path as its node values joined by `"->"`, for example `"1->2->5"`.
A leaf is a node with no children.
problems.title: Binary Tree Paths

problems.constraints:
- `2 <= n <= 15`
- `graph[i]` holds distinct nodes, never `i` itself, and the graph has no cycles
problems.statement:
A directed acyclic graph has nodes `0..n-1`; `graph[i]` lists the nodes reachable from node `i` by one edge. Return every path from node
`0` to node `n - 1`, in any order.
problems.title: All Paths From Source to Target

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= s.length <= 25`
- `s` has lowercase letters, `(` and `)`, with at most 20 parentheses
problems.statement:
`s` contains parentheses and lowercase letters. Remove the **minimum** number of parentheses so that the result is valid (every `(` has a
later matching `)`). Return every distinct result that achieves this minimum, in any order. Letters are never removed.
problems.title: Remove Invalid Parentheses

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= m, n <= 20`, `1 <= m * n <= 20`
- exactly one start and one end
problems.statement:
In the grid, `1` is the start, `2` is the end, `0` is an empty square you may walk on and `-1` is an obstacle. Moving up, down, left or right,
count the walks from start to end that visit **every non-obstacle square exactly once**.
problems.title: Unique Paths III

tests.explanation: No walk covers both empty squares.

problems.statement:
Place `n` queens on an `n x n` board so that no two attack each other. Return every distinct placement, in any order. Describe a board as `n`
strings, one per row, using `'Q'` for a queen and `'.'` for an empty square.
problems.title: N-Queens

problems.constraints: - `1 <= k <= n <= 20` (tests keep the output small)
problems.statement: Return every way to choose `k` distinct numbers from `1..n`, in any order (each combination's numbers may be in any order too).
problems.title: Combinations

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= beginWord.length <= 5`, all words have the same length
- `1 <= wordList.length <= 500`, words are distinct
- words consist of lowercase English letters, and `beginWord != endWord`
problems.statement:
A *transformation sequence* from `beginWord` to `endWord` is a list of words starting with `beginWord` where each next word differs from
the previous one in exactly one letter and belongs to `wordList` (`beginWord` itself doesn't need to be in `wordList`).

Return **all** shortest transformation sequences from `beginWord` to `endWord`, in any order, or an empty list if there is none.
problems.title: Word Ladder II

tests.explanation: hit -> hot -> dot -> dog -> cog and hit -> hot -> lot -> log -> cog.

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= currentState.length <= 500`
- `currentState[i]` is `'+'` or `'-'`
problems.statement:
In the Flip Game, a string contains only `'+'` and `'-'`. One move flips two consecutive `"++"` into `"--"`. Return every state that can be
reached from `currentState` with exactly one move, in any order (an empty list if no move is possible).
problems.title: Flip Game

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= num.length <= 35`
- `num` consists of digits
problems.statement:
A string of digits is *additive* if it can be split into at least three numbers where each number after the first two is the sum of the two
before it. Numbers in the sequence can't have leading zeros (`"0"` itself is fine, `"03"` isn't).

Return `true` if `num` is additive.
problems.title: Additive Number

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= candidates.length <= 100`
- `1 <= candidates[i] <= 50`
- `1 <= target <= 30`
problems.statement:
Given a list of positive integers `candidates` (which may contain duplicates) and a `target`, return every **distinct** combination of
candidates that adds up to `target`. Each candidate may be used at most once, and combinations are compared as multisets, so the answer never
lists the same combination twice. Any order is accepted.
problems.title: Combination Sum II
